question.text: In the anatomy of an AIF constitution, what is the CORRECT sequence of foundational documents/parties for an AIF set up as a trust?

answer.text: Settlor executes the Trust Deed with the Trustee; Trustee executes the Investment Management Agreement with the Manager; PPM is then filed with SEBI through a merchant banker
PPM is executed first, then the Trust Deed, then the IMA, then SEBI registration
SEBI registration is obtained first; Trust Deed is executed after SEBI grants registration
Investors subscribe via PPM; thereafter the Trust Deed is executed and the Manager is appointed

explanation.text: The Logic: The typical sequence is: (1) Settlor executes the Trust Deed appointing the Trustee and setting up the trust. (2) Trustee enters into an Investment Management Agreement (IMA) with the Manager. (3) The Fund applies for SEBI registration through a merchant banker and files the PPM. (4) Only after registration and PPM approval are investors solicited. The Trap: The trust must exist BEFORE it can contract a manager, and both must exist before SEBI registration can be sought. PPM cannot precede the trust's existence. Options A, C, D all invert the sequence. Cross-Exam Context: Same constitutional anatomy tested in XIX-A/B/C/D. XXI-B has an analogous PMS constitutional chain. Manager's Pro-Tip: In practice, draft the Trust Deed and IMA in parallel with PPM drafting, so the merchant banker can file a complete packet to SEBI. SEBI observations on PPM often trigger downstream amendments to IMA terms.
